💡 Progressive Delegation vs Continuous Heavy AI

Traditional CCTV systems continuously run heavy neural networks on every frame (25–30 FPS), consuming immense wattage and overheating edge hardware during static border hours.
IBVAP V1 Advantage: Engine 1 processes raw frames in sub-millisecond OpenCV time and filters out static scenes. Engine 2 is invoked strictly when meaningful movement occurs, slashing AI computation by up to 80-95%.

System Architecture & Operational Pipeline

Understanding the end-to-end data flow from camera frame acquisition to operator notification.

1. Ingestion (M1)

RTSP / File stream read into in-memory FramePackets. Bounded 90-frame ring buffer maintains pre-motion context.

→

2. Motion Gate (M2)

Engine 1 OpenCV differencing and contour clustering. Static frames are suppressed immediately.

→

3. Heavy AI (M3)

Core Orchestrator forwards motion ROI to Engine 2. YOLOv8 identifies HUMAN & VEHICLE targets.

→

4. Evidence Clip (M4)

Pre-motion buffer + trigger frame + post-motion frames are assembled into an MP4 clip.

→

5. Operator UI (M4)

FastAPI pushes real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE) to this Neumorphic Dashboard.

Why Not Save Full Video?

Border cameras run 24/7. Saving hundreds of hours of empty fence lines exhausts local disk space. IBVAP records only short bounded event clips centered on detected activity.

How Does Alert Cooldown Work?

A human walking across a camera takes 10–20 seconds. Instead of bombarding the operator with 30 alerts per second, the AlertManager applies a configurable cooldown (e.g. 5s) per camera/target.

Offline Independence

IBVAP V1 operates 100% locally on the edge machine. Model weights (`yolov8n.pt`), SQLite database, and video processing require zero external cloud connectivity.
